messages:
customer_john: hi support, we started getting NXDOMAIN for svc.billing.prod.redwood.internal from our prod pods after we peered the billing-vpc this morning. API errors across the board.

support_amy: thanks — can you paste a dig from one of the affected pods (include the server IP it hits)? also did you change any resolver/forwarder rules or security groups when peering?

customer_john: here's a dig from a pod on node-42: 
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc.billing.prod.redwood.internal @169.254.20.10 +short

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 40123
;; flags: qr aa rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1

customer_john: also ran dig +trace, top-level ends at our account resolver and then NXDOMAIN. No SERVFAILs.

infra_bot: Route53 change detected: private hosted zone "svc.billing.prod.redwood.internal" associated with VPC vpc-0b12345 (billing-account) at 2026-03-17T09:12:03Z (change-id /change/C123456)

support_amy: that infra_bot message is interesting — did the peering or automation accidentally associate a private hosted zone in the billing account that shadows the prod one? if two private hosted zones share the same name across accounts/VPCs you can get split-horizon behavior depending on resolver order.

dns_sre_liz: quick triage checklist: 
- confirm how the pod's stub resolver is configured (node-local? /etc/resolv.conf)
- check AWS: aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name and list-vpc-association-authorizations for duplicate zones
- check resolver rules/priority if you're using Outbound/Inboud endpoints
- flush node-local dns cache or restart node-local pods to rule out cached NXDOMAIN

support_amy: can you run these two commands and paste outputs? 
1) kubectl -n kube-system exec -it $(kubectl get po -n kube-system -l k8s-app=node-local-dns -o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}") -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
2) aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname svc.billing.prod.redwood.internal

customer_john: pasted outputs: 
/etc/resolv.conf -> nameserver 169.254.20.10

aws output: 
{ "HostedZones": [ { "Id": "/hostedzone/ZPROD1", "Name": "svc.billing.prod.redwood.internal.", "Config": { "PrivateZone": true }, "VPCs": [ { "VPCRegion": "us-east-1", "VPCId": "vpc-0a11111", "Account": "prod-account" } ] }, { "Id": "/hostedzone/ZBILL1", "Name": "svc.billing.prod.redwood.internal.", "Config": { "PrivateZone": true }, "VPCs": [ { "VPCRegion": "us-east-1", "VPCId": "vpc-0b12345", "Account": "billing-account" } ] } ] }

customer_john: seems there are two private hosted zones with identical names in two accounts and both are associated to VPCs we now have peered.

dns_sre_liz: yep that's the smoking gun. When two private zones with the same name exist, the resolver behavior depends on the resolver rules and VPC association order — peering can surface the shadowed zone and return NXDOMAIN if the zone has no records for that name in that account.

oncall_matt: also confirm that VPC resolver rule priority and inbound endpoint settings aren't forcing queries to the other account. if you're using a Resolver endpoint or forwarding rule to a central resolver, an overlapping private zone can still shadow.

support_amy: remediation options: 
- remove the unintended hosted zone association (disassociate VPC) in the billing account OR
- merge the records needed into the billing account zone OR
- add a higher-priority resolver rule that points queries for that domain to prod's resolver.

customer_john: we disassociated the billing-account hosted zone from the peered VPC (aws route53disassociate-vpc --hosted-zone-id ZBILL1 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0b12345) and restarted node-local-dns pods.

customer_john: after flush + restart dig now returns the A record: 10.2.3.21

support_amy: awesome — can you confirm application health? any lingering 5xx or cache issues?

customer_john: app errors cleared after a few minutes. no more NXDOMAIN.

dns_sre_liz: follow-ups to prevent recurrence: 
- add a preflight check in the peering automation to detect private hosted zone name collisions across accounts
- document who owns each private hosted zone and require explicit approval for cross-account association
- consider resolver rules that prefer prod's resolver for svc.billing.prod.redwood.internal

oncall_matt: noted — I'll open a ticket with infra to add a guardrail.

support_amy: glad we got you unblocked. closing the thread once you confirm no regressions. :tada:

customer_john: confirming stable over 20m. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
